# Throughput campaign — final native evidence

The original regular-load throughput target passed this finite screen. Final candidate pooled throughput was **81.252 versus ARC 80.806 output tokens/s (+0.552%)**, and all six prospectively paired regular comparisons were positive (+0.103% to +2.064%). The −0.2% fallback was not needed for regular throughput. This is measured sample performance, not statistical equivalence or proof that the new option caused a speedup.

Broader confirmation is mixed: the three higher-concurrency pairs pooled to **−0.168%**, with individual cells −1.588%, +1.197%, −0.066%. One regular pair missed the prospectively declared engineering latency screen: median first-token latency +16.480% for seed1103 pair2 (cell pooled median +7.743%). Mean/background TTFT in that pair rose +2.064%/+1.167%. Thus **regular throughput passed; universal parity and every latency screen did not**. No adverse run was discarded or retuned.

## Change and causal evidence

New experimental, default-off `prefetch_preserve_gpu_prefix_cache=true` permits speculative allocation only from the contiguous unhashed head of the native free-block queue. Native reclaimable “free” blocks can still contain reusable cached prefix entries; ordinary `get_new_blocks` erases those hashes. The same conservative capacity feeds wait reservation, coalescing, competition and legacy staging. Native demand allocation, free order, refcounts, scoring, query capture, fences, geometry and admission remain unchanged. Unsupported queue layouts fail closed; caching-disabled pools keep normal capacity.

The six-arm allocator screen confirmed **8 directly erased cached blocks/run with old staging, 0 with the new option**. Safe staging still completed and consumed one actual 2.25MiB block/run, versus seven consumed with old staging. This prevents direct speculative cache destruction at the cost of lower prefetch coverage. Reserved scratch can still cause indirect pressure. No VRAM-capacity or production-benefit claim follows.

The historical 2–3% throughput loss was not reproduced: old staging itself exceeded ARC by +0.374%/+0.398% in the new screen. All arms retained the historical agent4-turn2 1456-token GPU prefix there. The ledger does not observe cache republication, so an old removal does not prove a counterfactual miss. The historical tail mechanism remains unproved; do not attribute the full regular throughput result causally to this patch.

## Frozen protocol

Qwen3-4B dense BF16 TP1 eager, same protected runtime/model revisions, 640 GPU blocks (1440MiB), 448MiB/199 DRAM blocks, store threshold2, staging cap192 inside the same GPU pool, ARC retention, opportunity schedule/stride8/flat, native adoption unchanged, soft retention off, owned reclaimable staging, causal pending-tool hints with fixed250ms estimate. Six agent sessions plus12 background requests:45 requests/3264 greedy outputs per arm. PYTHONHASHSEED4109 throughout. Different trace seeds change only the frozen causal workload process, not policy access to future waits/results/abandonment.

Initial screen: ARC/old/safe/safe/old/ARC, same bounded passive allocator ledger in every arm. Confirmation: three seeds4109/1103/3301, two balanced regular pairs each at maxseq3, one alternating pair each at maxseq4. All source/runtime profilers off; original identical compact hooks in confirmation without the allocator ledger. Closed-loop completion changes subsequent release and cache histories; background arrivals stay open-loop. Throughput is all completed output tokens divided by intended load-start to last completion. No repeated samples were selected after seeing outcomes.

*Capture counts are lifecycle aggregates including warmup; bounded first batches independently identify captures from actual timed requests. ARC legitimately has capture disabled; every candidate retains real semantic query capture. Organic scoring jobs/rankings were zero in these product workloads, so no serving ranking-value or index benefit is claimed. The native CPU constrained competition test uses real tensor scores and the real metadata/consumer path, not invented ratings.

Confirmation completed **810/810 requests, 58,752 exact output tokens, 109,254 exact native ordered-key recurrences**. Combined with the initial screen:1080 requests/78,336 outputs exact. All transfer jobs succeeded; no request failures, OOMs, prefetch allocation failures or preemptions. Candidate confirmation consumed8 real blocks/18MiB,6blocks/13.5MiB ready by intended demand release; no observed unused speculative bytes. All regular candidate arms consumed a real prefetched block; two concurrent seeds had no eligible consumed opportunity. The native GPU/DRAM pool budgets were not enlarged.

Full per-request release/submit TTFT, request elapsed, mean ITL, intended release offsets, hit/admission/prompt-work tokens, H2D/D2H/splice, concurrency and native identities are in confirmation/measurements.csv. Full session last-completion/cache/prompt-work counters, pool samples, allocator peaks, stage-ready/consume/fence validation and explicit postload state are in evidence JSON. Pool snapshots are sampled, not a time-weighted occupancy integral; whole-run allocator peaks include startup. API/host envelopes are not isolated DMA or GPU compute durations. No new GPU utilization claim is made from wall time.

## Adverse cells and limits

For concurrency seed4109, candidate executes79,443 prompt tokens versus ARC85,443 but finishes0.585s later; agent4 is the last session in both. Large closed-loop cache/release differences occur across several sessions, including agent1 −1296 GPU-hit tokens/+1280 prompt tokens at index9, while other requests gain hits. Fewer total prompt tokens do not ensure a shorter critical tail. This unprofiled one-pair stress cell does not identify the root cause or establish repeatability.

For regular seed1103 pair2, ARC takes an alternate closed-loop cache/scheduling path:79,433 executed prompt tokens versus candidate85,753, with different releases and cache hits across multiple sessions. ARC median TTFT is lower but its final completion is0.855s later. Candidate’s other seed1103 regular pair has +0.195% median TTFT and +0.202% throughput. The adverse median is retained; it is not dismissed as proven noise.

One ARC concurrency seed1103 server logged AsyncLLM EngineDeadError during teardown after engine-manager shutdown; all45 requests, explicit export and transfers had already completed, the server exited0 and the owned tree was empty. This shutdown anomaly is preserved in the raw log. No serving failure is hidden by counting only successful requests.

Two regular pairs per seed and one stress pair per seed provide observed ranges, not statistical equivalence. No long-history extension or production trace was measured. Regular paired throughput range is +0.103%..+2.064%; stress range −1.588%..+1.197%. Original regular target is met in these observations; broader all-workload parity and all chosen latency gates are not established. Further speculative capture/index/summary optimizations are not justified by these zero-score product results. Root independently reviews evidence and decides integration; no training message has been sent.

## Correctness, provenance and cleanup

374 native CPU tests pass with CUDA initialization forbidden, including seven new allocator/semantic integration fixtures. The exact new gate preserves native hash/LRU/refcount behavior and default behavior. Real ARC scheduler → request branch → metadata → worker CPU tensor scoring → final constrained prefix winner is covered, with only hardware transfer construction stubbed. Existing generation/TTL/residency/duplicate/reset/ownership tests remain. Native serving checks actual transferred keys, reserved/adopted physical destinations, completion fences, worker use and exact outputs. No GPU math/kernel change required a new synthetic CUDA fixture.

Initial prep assertion and one stale SimpleNamespace test-fixture failure are retained, followed by the corrected374-pass suite. Supplement analysis first failed on ARC’s absent async_stats (None); only null handling in the post-run analysis was repaired, without changing measured source/hooks/inputs. All frozen source/config/hook pins, original source/runtime pins and207 prior round4 manifest entries reverify. Production delta vs round4 is connector.py only; tests add coverage. Default option is false.

Latest user replacement AGENTS removed checkout gating and expressly directed execution after actual live-work checks. Runs used direct finite project supervision, not a claimed broker grant: one serial180s-bounded model lifecycle at a time, existing project lock, subreaper-owned descendant cleanup. No broker/shared setting changes, downloads/builds, other-owner interruption, commits or pushes. The prior stale request was left untouched. All27 direct receipts have empty owned trees; project lock is free; final actual GPU check shows no compute processes. No further GPU work is scheduled.

Archive, source/deltas, exact pins and reproduction instructions are linked in HANDOFF.md. Separate post-archive cleanup/export/notification receipts remain outside the immutable main archive. Protected models/environment/runtime/shared worker/prior results are retained; storage-steward records native Windows and WSL free bytes separately. Root owns final acceptance/Mac integration and the conditional training handoff.

## Root acceptance and integration

The Mac independently verified the compact review archive, file lengths, absolute paired throughput ratios, native cleanup receipts and exact production pins. Regular pooled throughput recomputes to +0.552281%; all six pairs are positive. The stated regular-throughput objective is accepted for this finite screen. Stress and latency exceptions, zero organic scoring jobs, limited repeatability and unproved patch causality remain explicit above.

The exact measured connector is integrated with the documented default-off option. Test helpers now use repository package imports; their bytes match a separate CUDA-forbidden native rerun with374passing tests. Mac additionally passed syntax, six actual-method CPU smoke cases and diff whitespace checks; the full runtime suite was run on WSL, not Mac. No commits or pushes. See ROOT-REVIEW.json, INTEGRATION.json and STORAGE.json.
